speaker: Swami Sivananda
title: Elevating the mind with prayer and hymns
text: Get by heart some prayer – Slokas (prayer verses), Stotras (hymns) and repeat them as soon as you sit in the Asana before starting Japa or meditation. This will elevate the mind quickly.
modern_interpretation: Before engaging in focused mental work, mindfulness, or meditation, commit to memory and recite a few uplifting affirmations, sacred verses, or inspirational chants. Performing this short ritual right as you settle into your dedicated practice space helps to swiftly calm mental chatter, shift your mindset, and prepare your consciousness for deeper concentration and inner peace.
summary: Swami Sivananda advises memorizing prayers or hymns and repeating them before beginning Japa or meditation. This simple practice serves to swiftly elevate and prepare the mind for deeper spiritual engagement.
actionable_advice: Before starting any focused task or meditation, choose a short positive affirmation or spiritual verse and quietly repeat it a few times to center and calm your mind.
embedding_ready_text: Swami Sivananda advises memorizing and reciting prayers, slokas, or hymns immediately before beginning Japa or meditation. This powerful practice is designed to quickly elevate and calm a restless mind, preparing it for deeper spiritual engagement and fostering a strong spiritual connection. Modernly, this translates to using short, positive affirmations or spiritual verses as a pre-focus ritual to overcome mental distraction, reduce pre-meditation anxiety, and cultivate immediate clarity and inner peace, enhancing your overall mental readiness and deepening your spiritual practice.
